newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper/aluminium stocks seen down, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: LME copper/aluminium stocks seen down, trade quiet.

text.p: Far East traders said they expect London Metal Exchange (LME) copper and aluminium stocks figures to show a dip later on Tuesday, while regional base metals business remains sluggish.
Copper stocks will probably drop by 2,000-4,000 tonnes while aluminium inventories are likely to fall by between 5,000-9,000 tonnes in the LME report to be released at 0900 GMT, they said.
"Everybody says copper will be down about 2,000 to 4,000 tonnes. Ally (aluminium) could be 5,000-7,000 tonnes down," a senior trader for a European metal trading house said.
Metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review there were rumours in the market that aluminium stocks "would fall by 6,000 to 9,000 tonnes."
"The consensus seems to be for copper and aluminium to head lower," a dealer in a Singapore-based trading house added.
Business around the region remained quiet while there were no reports of any fresh shipments of copper arriving in the LME's Singapore warehouses.
"There's no upsurge in demand for copper around here," one dealer said, adding copper inventories in the LME store in the city state will probably remain steady.

"We haven't seen or heard of any substantial material coming in lately," another dealer said. The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 54,975 tonnes in the exchange's stock report last Friday, down 1,050 tonnes from the previous Tuesday's report.
Three-month copper was quoted by regional traders at 0330 GMT at around US$2,407/12 a tonne against the late quote in London on Monday of $2,408 a tonne.
Three-month aluminium was pegged at 0330 GMT at about $1,688/93 a tonne compared with late trade in London yesterday of $1,689 a tonne, the dealers said.
